cells.tense: You are at the table where endings get decided and you are deciding one now.
cells.ask: Tell the person it touches what you are keeping and what you are setting down, in the same breath. Their answer can change your mind.
cells.core:
You still know how to do this part. When something in your care has run its course, you set it down, and there is room afterward that was not there before. A project gets closed and something better takes the space. A way of doing things gets put away and a person can finally breathe. The people close to you have felt this, and they trust it coming from you.

The invitation this carries is that you are free to keep feeding what is growing instead of guarding what is finished. That motion runs through you and lands on somebody. Ask for something back in the same motion. Fairness here is not a scoreboard. It is what keeps this from becoming a load you carry alone.
cells.sheetLine: You end what is finished and something else gets room.
cells.verb: releasing what is finished and turning it into ground for what comes next
cells.place: where something is being tended toward what it is becoming

cells.tense: You are steering toward a version of this that has not arrived yet, and it has your full attention.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you have been steering hard and leave it alone for a week. Tell someone you are doing it on purpose so your hands stay off it.
cells.core:
You can see what this is supposed to become, and that picture has gotten ahead of the thing itself. Something still forming gets treated like it should already be further along. A small trim starts to feel urgent, and when it does not move faster, you look for a shape to force it into. Nothing here is careless. The clock is just yours, and it runs ahead of the growth.

The cost is that the growing thing stops being able to surprise you, because you have already decided what it is going to be. The way out is giving it room, which means you stepping back, not it growing faster. Leave it a while. Come back after the time has done part of the work.

cells.tense: You have stopped taking things up and you are waiting in the place where you stopped.
cells.ask: Pick the smallest thing in your care and do one concrete act for it today. Tell one person you did it and leave it there.
cells.core:
Things in your care need a hand and your hand is not going out to them. Not coldness — a stall. Deciding what to keep and what to end stopped seeming worth the trouble, so neither happens. What is growing waits, and that waiting is also an answer it is getting from you.

What is thin here is not the caring. It is the willingness to move first. Do one small, visible thing for something that is actually growing, and let that be enough for now. If nothing answers, the move was still yours and it still counts. That is not throwing yourself at the work. It is one foot on the floor.

cells.tense: You do the choosing in this place and describe it as things working themselves out.
cells.ask: Name one call you made that changed what grew here, one sentence, to the person it touched. Not the version where it simply happened.
cells.core:
Things pass through your hands — what gets held, what gets ended, what is allowed to continue — and you say it turned out the way it turned out. You have been redirecting what was headed wrong and calling it the way things went. Someone in the room watched you do it.

Saying it plainly is not for credit. Someone near you may be waiting to hear that the call was yours, so they can lean on it or argue with it. Either is more useful than luck. There is no new skill here. Own one decision, and see how much clearer the next one comes.
